cases.sentence: Плавностью движений, мягкостью и гибкостью ___ и несколько хитрою и сдержанною манерой она напоминала красивого, но еще не сформировавшегося котенка, который будет прелестною кошечкой.
cases.explain: «маленьких членов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The only young people remaining in the drawing room, not counting the young lady visitor and the countess’ eldest daughter (who was four years older than her sister and behaved already like a grown-up person), were Nikoláy and Sónya, the niece. Sónya was a slender little brunette with a tender look in her eyes which were veiled by long lashes, thick black plaits coiling twice round her head, and a tawny tint in her complexion and especially in the color of her slender but graceful and muscular arms and neck. By the grace of her movements, by the softness and flexibility of her small limbs, and by a certain coyness and reserve of manner, she reminded one of a pretty, half-grown kitten which promises to become a beautiful little cat. She evidently considered it proper to show an interest in the general conversation by smiling, but in spite of herself her eyes under their thick long lashes watched her cousin who was going to join the army, with such passionate girlish adoration that her smile could not for a single instant impose upon anyone, and it was clear that the kitten had settled down only to spring up with more energy and again play with her cousin as soon as they too could, like Natásha and Borís, escape from the drawing room.

cases.sentence: — Да, ma chère, — сказал ___, обращаясь к гостье и указывая на своего Николая.
cases.explain: «старый граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ah yes, my dear,” said the count, addressing the visitor and pointing to Nikoláy, “his friend Borís has become an officer, and so for friendship’s sake he is leaving the university and me, his old father, and entering the military service, my dear. And there was a place and everything waiting for him in the Archives Department! Isn’t that friendship?” remarked the count in an inquiring tone.

cases.sentence: — Совсем не дружба, а просто чувствую призвание к ___.
cases.explain: «военной службе» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “It’s not at all from friendship,” declared Nikoláy, flaring up and turning away as if from a shameful aspersion. “It is not from friendship at all; I simply feel that the army is my vocation.”

cases.explain: «старый граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “All right, all right!” said the old count. “He always flares up! This Bonaparte has turned all their heads; they all think of how he rose from an ensign and became Emperor. Well, well, God grant it,” he added, not noticing his visitor’s sarcastic smile.

cases.sentence: Он выждал ___ разговора и с расстроенным лицом вышел из комнаты отыскивать Соню.
cases.explain: «первый перерыв» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The young man, flattered, sat down nearer to her with a coquettish smile, and engaged the smiling Julie in a confidential conversation without at all noticing that his involuntary smile had stabbed the heart of Sónya, who blushed and smiled unnaturally. In the midst of his talk he glanced round at her. She gave him a passionately angry glance, and hardly able to restrain her tears and maintain the artificial smile on her lips, she got up and left the room. All Nikoláy’s animation vanished. He waited for the first pause in the conversation, and then with a distressed face left the room to find Sónya.

cases.sentence: — Как секреты-то этой всей молодежи шиты ___!
cases.explain: «белыми нитками» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “How plainly all these young people wear their hearts on their sleeves!” said Anna Mikháylovna, pointing to Nikoláy as he went out. “Cousinage—dangereux voisinage,”3 she added.

cases.sentence: — Да, сказала графиня, после того как луч солнца, проникнувший в гостиную вместе с этим ___, исчез, и как будто отвечая на вопрос, которого никто ей не делал, но который постоянно занимал ее.
cases.explain: «молодым поколением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Yes,” said the countess when the brightness these young people had brought into the room had vanished; and as if answering a question no one had put but which was always in her mind, “and how much suffering, how much anxiety one has had to go through that we might rejoice in them now! And yet really the anxiety is greater now than the joy. One is always, always anxious! Especially just at this age, so dangerous both for girls and boys.”

cases.sentence: — Я знаю, что я всегда буду первою confidente[130] советницей моих дочерей, и что Николинька, по своему ___, ежели будет шалить (мальчику нельзя без этого), то всё не так, как эти петербургские господа.
cases.explain: «пылкому характеру» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Yes, you’re quite right,” continued the countess. “Till now I have always, thank God, been my children’s friend and had their full confidence,” said she, repeating the mistake of so many parents who imagine that their children have no secrets from them. “I know I shall always be my daughters’ first confidante, and that if Nikólenka, with his impulsive nature, does get into mischief (a boy can’t help it), he will all the same never be like those Petersburg young men.”

cases.explain: «милое существо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What a charming creature your younger girl is,” said the visitor; “a little volcano!”

cases.sentence: — Всегда с ___ мудрят, хотят сделать что-нибудь необыкновенное, — сказала гостья.
cases.explain: «старшими детьми» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “People are always too clever with their eldest children and try to make something exceptional of them,” said the visitor.
